subject: Money
title: Cattle as Currency
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cattle as Currency.

hook.text: The word 'pecuniary' comes from Latin pecus, meaning cattle. Cows were literally capital.

buildup.text: In ancient Rome and India, wealth was measured in herds. Cattle provided milk, meat, and labor.

discovery.text: Cattle money had a problem: you can't make change. Try splitting a cow for a small purchase.

twist.text: The Maasai still measure wealth in cattle today. A rich man might own 1,000 head and no cash.

climax.text: Cattle were money because they were universally valued. Money is always what everyone wants.

punchline.text: The first bank accounts had hooves.

quiz.question: What Latin word for cattle gives us 'pecuniary'?
